kicker: PyTorch on TPUs, as a device

scenes.headline: How TorchTPU makes a TPU a PyTorch device
scenes.sub: Google and Meta's new backend, read from the code
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Grommet! TorchTPU runs ordinary PyTorch on Google's TPUs, as a real device.

scenes.text: Every ATen op gets a TPU kernel that builds StableHLO, and a policy decides when those ops are compiled and launched.
scenes.say: The idea: every op gets a TPU kernel, and a policy decides when to compile and launch.

left.title: Lazy tensors
items: Every op records into a graph
A new shape means a new compile
left.say: The old path recorded ops into a graph and compiled at a step boundary you marked.

right.title: A PyTorch device
items: Each op has a TPU kernel
right.say: TorchTPU is a device in the dispatcher. Eager runs op by op; deferring is a choice.

scenes.title: One op, from Python to the chip

steps.say: An op on a tpu tensor reaches a kernel registered under the private use key.
That kernel builds a tiny StableHLO function. There are about four hundred and forty.
In defer and fuse mode nothing runs. The tensor points at a deferred op.
When Python reads a value, the region it needs becomes a cache key.
A miss compiles once. A hit launches the cached program on the TPU.

items.say: Strict launches each op and lets the CPU run ahead.
Defer and fuse waits for a read, then runs one fused program.
Torch compile replays a whole graph through the same deferral.

steps.say: PyTorch and JAX both emit StableHLO. Pallas kernels enter lower, as Mosaic.
Below that is one XLA compiler, down to a TPU executable.

scenes.title: One run, two MFU figures
scenes.say: The numbers check out, with a catch. Two posts quote different efficiency for one run: one charges attention for the half a causal mask skips.

scenes.text: The new part is a policy: when to compile. Eager, deferred and compiled modes share one lowering.
scenes.say: Remember: the new part is when to compile, and every mode shares one lowering.
